Definition: from G1212; to make plain (by words):--declare, shew, signify.
BiblicalUsage: To declare is to make plain by words, and the word gathers the declaring of the gospel: the report brought to Paul, the witness of the prophets, and the declaration of the end from the beginning. The apostles declare what they have seen and heard, and the Lord declares what will be.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe declaring is the work of the witness: we do not invent the message, we make plain what God has shown. The declaring is the plain telling of what God has done, and the telling is the witness.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
